text:
Sam (Support): FYI dropped-in a customer escalation — ACME reported a surge of 429s and a billing anomaly when they hit our rwd-4x-32k model with very long contexts. Copying logs and repro below.

Priya (SRE): thanks — can you paste the raw responses / headers? We need to know if these are throttles (Retry-After) or auth failures.

Sam (Support): pasted from the customer's dump (redacted token):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2026 14:22:11 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit-Model-RPM: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining-Model-RPM: 0
X-RateLimit-Limit-Model-TPM: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining-Model-TPM: 15
Retry-After: 6
{
  "error": {"message":"model rate limit exceeded for rwd-4x-32k","type":"rate_limit_error"}
}
```
They said this happened mid-burst after ~90s of sustained traffic, with ~18 concurrent connections using our SDK default backoff. They also noticed a spike in their overage billing entries mirroring the time range.

Marta (Eng): interesting — that header naming is what our per-model quota enforcement emits for hosted API. Two quick hypotheses: 1) per-minute RPM pegged (120 RPM) because requests are heavy (each request had large context length) — model CPU->quota accounting scales with effective token-equivalent weight; 2) concurrency/cumulative active requests triggered the runtime-level soft throttle which replies 429s with Retry-After instead of queueing.

Priya (SRE): can we confirm whether long context was the root cause? Do we log context length or token_count on the request metadata?

Marta (Eng): yes, we log a token_count estimator for every request. I checked the live traces for ACME's org_id (redacted) — average input_tokens ~ 18k, output_tokens ~ 2k, so 20k tokens/request. That effectively multiplies their RPM/TPM usage. If our per-model RPM is fixed (120 RPM), each heavy request counts the same as a small one unless we apply per-token metering rules — currently we meter per request + per-token for billing but the rate limiter uses request-weight buckets with token-weight amplification for extended contexts on rwd-4x-32k. I see the weight factor set to 8x for >16k input tokens.

Jules (Billing): the billing spike they saw aligns: requests were charged by token; the spike is expected. The customer is upset because they expected graceful queuing, not immediate 429s.

Sam (Support): customer wants: 1) explanation why 429s instead of queuing, 2) a repro they can run to validate, 3) help reducing cost and avoiding throttles short-term.

Priya (SRE): short answers: 1) we enforce per-model RPM/TPM caps to protect multi-tenant capacity. For heavy/contextual requests we apply a weight multiplier to prevent noisy neighbours. When bursts exceed capacity and no spare pods exist, the runtime returns 429 (soft throttle) with Retry-After. 2) repro below. 3) mitigation suggestions follow.

Sam (Support): adding the repro the customer used (sanitized):
```
# repro: 18 concurrent curl clients, each streaming a ~20k-token prompt
for i in $(seq 1 18); do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-4x-32k","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"...huge context..."},{"role":"user","content":"<20000 token payload>"}],"stream":false}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions &
done
wait
```
They also ran the request with our JS SDK (v1.3.2) with default retry/backoff and saw identical 429s after ~45s of sustained load.

Marta (Eng): reproduce looks good. Two action items for eng: 1) confirm multiplier configuration per model (I can see config but want to be explicit), 2) verify soft-throttle path returns correct Retry-After and logs org_id + token_count so support can map to billing entries.

Priya (SRE): I'll check runtime traces and pod metrics for that org in the time window. If we had a transient capacity shortage (pod lifecycle / autoscaler lag), that explains queueing -> immediate 429 behavior.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-8342, linked to thread. Assigned to Priya (SRE).

Marta (Eng): config excerpt (from staging-ish snippet, not production):
```
models:
  rwd-4x-32k:
    rpm_limit: 120
    tpm_limit: 6000
    concurrency_limit: 16
    long_context_weight_threshold_tokens: 16000
    long_context_weight_multiplier: 8
```
So when input_tokens > 16k, the request counts as 8 requests against RPM pool. With 18 concurrent clients each making ~1 req/sec they'd blow through RPM very fast.

Jules (Billing): ok that explains both 429s and the bill. Billing charged tokens correctly; the 8x weight doesn't affect token billing, only rate limiting. Customers often misunderstand that distinction.

Sam (Support): suggestions for customer to avoid repeat in short term?

Marta (Eng): short-term mitigation: - batch/prefix cache to cut repeated context - reduce concurrency to <=12 to stay under concurrency limit - switch to streaming/chunked prompts so each request has smaller input token window - or use our dedicated offering or request higher model quotas.

Priya (SRE): operational mitigation: we can tune autoscaler to spin up burst pods faster for orgs with sudden traffic (requires Dedicated or enterprise tier), and we can relax Retry-After semantics (longer queueing window) but that risks latency SLOs for other tenants.

Sam (Support): I drafted a message to ACME summarizing cause + steps. PTAL: 
"Hi — thanks for the repro, we investigated. Root cause: heavy long-context requests triggered our per-model weighted rate limiter for rwd-4x-32k (we count requests with >16k tokens as 8x). That exhausted the RPM bucket and caused 429s with Retry-After. Billing counts tokens as usual, so charges are expected for the requests you sent. Short-term options: lower concurrency, use streaming/chunking, enable prefix caching, or request increased quota/dedicated capacity. We're happy to open a quota request for you and offer a short-term credit while we work through options."

Marta (Eng): LGTM. Also add a small repro suggestion for them to validate locally: reduce the prompt to 8k tokens and re-run the 18 concurrent test — they should not hit the RPM limit then.

Jules (Billing): I'll propose a one-off credit covering the excess token charges during the incident window and attach a note explaining weighted throttles to avoid confusion.

Sam (Support): Customer replied: "thanks — will try the 8k test. can you confirm what our per-model concurrency/quota numbers are?"

Priya (SRE): we should share the official numbers: RPM 120, TPM 6000, concurrency_limit 16 for rwd-4x-32k (prod). But add: these are per-org soft limits; Dedicated customers can get different values. Also note the long-context multiplier.

Marta (Eng): I'll open a small docs PR to make the weighted-rate-limiter behavior visible in the model page and add an example showing how effective RPM changes with context size.

Priya (SRE): follow-ups for the team: 1) eng to validate prod config matches snippet and ensure logging (org_id + token_count + weight) is present, 2) support to send templated explanation + repro + mitigation steps + credit note, 3) billing to apply credit, 4) docs PR for transparency.

Sam (Support): assigning tasks: Priya -> runtime traces + config confirm; Marta -> docs PR + config verify; Jules -> credit; Sam -> customer comms and repro guide.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-8342 status: triaged -> investigating.

Priya (SRE): quick runtime note: if you see Retry-After but no X-RateLimit headers, that's likely an auth/edge ratelimit; in that case check their API key usage patterns. This thread shows clear X-RateLimit-Model headers so model quota is the culprit.

Sam (Support): closing loop — sending the draft to ACME now and adding the reproduction note. Will update thread when they confirm the 8k test. :thumbsup:
